All four CPTs return rest_no_route 404. show_in_rest=false is in effect.

findings.check: /manifest.json (no trailing slash) returns 200; /service-worker.js (no trailing slash) returns 200

results.notes: Without trailing slash returns 301 redirect (x-redirect-by: WordPress) to /manifest.json/. Follows successfully to 200. Browsers tolerate the redirect, but bare URL is not 200.

Hard nginx 404 on /service-worker.js. Only /service-worker.js/ (with trailing slash) returns 200. This is wrong for service workers — many registrations specify the bare path. Spec says SW must be served at the scope path it claims.

findings.evidence_curl_headers: manifest: HTTP/2 301; location: https://mantia3.wpcomstaging.com/manifest.json/. service-worker: HTTP/2 404 nginx, length 146.
findings.summary: manifest.json/no-slash: 301 (minor). service-worker.js/no-slash: 404 (high). Both fail the R3 paper-cut 'bare URLs work without trailing slash' bar.

findings.check: Competition page subtitle uses arrow '→' not en-dash '–'
findings.notes: Subtitle line uses the proper arrow. No stray dashes elsewhere on the page either.

new_observations.observation: HTML <link rel="manifest" href="https://mantia3.wpcomstaging.com/manifest.json/"> already includes the trailing slash, so PWA install in the browser works. The bare /manifest.json URL just isn't canonical.

/libertadores-2026/ (without /penca/ prefix) 404s into the default WordPress 'Page not found' template (not the themed mantia 404). Only /penca/<slug> is themed. Outside this is fine, but worth knowing for future deep-link shares.
